extracted.intended_audience: state agencies filing notices and members of the public who use the Texas Register / Texas Administrative Code (rule authors, notice filers, and commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting and using Texas Register postings, open meeting notices, and rulemaking materials (including comment periods, publication timing, and access to the Texas Administrative Code). Intended for agencies that post notices and members of the public who read/subscribe or comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open meeting submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Both state and regional agencies submit their notices of open meetings to the Secretary of State's office through a secure internet site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may post their meetings at any time and are not limited to posting during normal business hours. Meetings are added to the open meetings portion of the Texas Register internet site within five minutes of being posted by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for content of open meeting notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State is not responsible for the information or content that is contained in open meeting notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SOS makes no representations as to sufficiency or accuracy of the posted information; inquiries about a particular posting should be directed to the entity that submitted it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Register publication frequency and posting time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Register is published weekly, every Friday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue will be posted on the internet site by 5 p.m. CST every Friday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and currency of the Texas Administrative Code (TAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Administrative Code is current through today's date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can rely on the online TAC being up-to-date as of the date viewed (subject to any later filings/exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of graphic and tabular material online
rubrics_metrics.description: All graphic and tabular material in each issue of the Texas Register is included in all online services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic/tabular elements that appear in print are provided in the online versions; no additional conversion required for viewing those elements online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period / reasonable opportunity to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Texas Gov't Code 2001.029 states a state agency "...shall give all interested persons a reasonable opportunity to submit data, views, or arguments, orally or in writing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the general statutory standard for notice-and-comment; agencies must provide a reasonable opportunity for public participation consistent with this statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum delay before adopting a proposed rule (30‑day publication requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules may not be submitted to the Texas Register for adoption any earlier than 30 days from the date of publication of the proposed rule in the Texas Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must allow at least a 30-day period after publication before submitting the same text for adoption; this enforces a minimum notice interval to allow public response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule effective date timing and filing trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, a rule takes effect 20 days after the date on which it is filed with the Secretary of State. Day one is the date following the filing, and the rule may take effect on day 20. Note that the time period for an adopted rule is triggered by filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions under Texas Gov't Code 2001.036; agencies should consult that statute for any special effective-date rules (e.g., emergency rules or other exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rules and statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes are created or amended by the Legislature. Rules are adopted by state agencies (Executive branch), usually with specific rulemaking authority from the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding this distinction helps users know why agencies issue rules and where statutory authority for rulemaking is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source responsibility and contact information for posted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The postings contained in the Texas Register are submitted electronically by parties outside the control of the SOS and any questions about a particular posting should be directed to that entity. Contact information is included in each posted document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because postings originate with submitting entities, readers should use the included contact details to resolve content questions rather than relying on SOS to correct or verify submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and access options for the Texas Register
rubrics_metrics.description: For print subscriptions, contact LexisNexis Matthew Bender & Company at 800-223-1940. For access to internet-based services, call the Texas Register at (512) 463-5561 or email register@sos.texas.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural contact points for obtaining print or online access to the Texas Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain printable copies of TAC chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of individual chapters can be downloaded for free in a variety of formats by using our Public Document Request option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users seeking offline or printable copies should use the Public Document Request service to obtain chapters in preferred formats.
